2017_108_060617mtg.paragraph: Agenda packet for the Troy Board of Education regular meeting of June 6, 2017 at Athens High School. The night is built around student recognition — 69 lettered items covering the winter All-State athletes, the 2016-2017 senior scholar athletes and a Youth Recognition deck spanning every academic and arts competition the district entered. The business is thin by comparison: a consent agenda carrying four sets of minutes and the second reading of five board policies, a resolution setting the 2017-2018 budget public hearing for June 20, 2017, and a bond update reporting Series 1 construction 98% complete against a $125.7 M program.

**Meeting**
Regular meeting, June 6, 2017, 7:00 PM, Athens High School, 4333 John R. Agenda: Pledge of Allegiance; Recognition (items A through OOO); Additions & Deletions; Public Communication (agenda items); General – Consent Agenda; Personnel; Curriculum; Business; Public Communication (non-agenda items); Other; Adjournment.

**Recognition**
Mike Jolly reads the two athletics items. 2.A names the All-State Athletes for Winter 2017 — twenty-three students, overwhelmingly Troy High synchronized swimmers, plus bowling, gymnastics and boys swim. 2.B lists the Senior Scholar Athletes for 2016-2017 who carried a 3.5 grade point average, an extended roster across both high schools. The remaining 67 items form the 2016-2017 Board of Education Youth Recognition deck, each naming the students and their advisor. Among the results: Boulan Park first in the nation in the American Mathematics Competition and International Academy East first in state and national; second in the nation in the American Scholastic League; first place team and an individual gold medal at the International Math Olympiad; Destination Imagination teams from Schroeder Elementary, Smith, Boulan Park, IA-East and Athens advancing to Global Finals, with Larson taking third place internationally at the European Invitational; FIRST Robotics world championship teams from Athens and Troy High, with Dikshant Sharma a Dean's List winner; second in the nation in the National Language Arts League; first in state and second in the nation in the Purple Comet Math Contest; and national finalists in the MIT INSPIRE competition, Genes in Space and the Siemens research competition.

**Consent agenda**
Minutes of the May 2 workshop, the May 16 meeting, and the May 23 special and closed sessions, plus second reading and adoption of five board policies: 2000.04 School District Clubs & Other Activities, 4000.01 Personnel – Labor Negotiation Team, 5000.03 Purchasing – Competitive Bidding & Micro-Purchases, 6000.02 Safety & Security – Firearms & Other Weapons, and 8000.09 General Policies – Web Accessibility. The Board Policy Committee and the Board's attorney reviewed them for compliance with State law, the Open Meetings Act and the Revised School Code; the first reading was May 16.

**What the attached minutes record**
The May 16 meeting honored teachers Erin Detmer and Natalie Haezebrouck for acceptance into the Teachers' College at Columbia University August Writing Institute, named Erin Prendergast the Outstanding Support Staff Employee of the Year from sixteen nominees, and recognized twenty-six retirees — among them Gary Griffith of Troy High, a dedicated employee since 1974. It also recorded a $10,000 AT&T Foundation grant, secured through the Troy Community Foundation and Oakland County Commissioner Doug Tietz, funding transportation for high school students in after-school tutoring, and the Troy Foundation for Educational Excellence's 80 grants for the year.

Three actions passed 5-0 with Miletti and Philippart absent: Jessica Carrier as Special Education Supervisor effective July 1, 2017; Elizabeth Soggs as Director of Technology effective June 5, 2017; and a copier lease authorizing a Master Equipment Lease Agreement with Great America Financial Services for no more than four years at an annual cost not to exceed $63,690.48, plus a cost-per-copy maintenance agreement with Applied Imaging at not more than $.0032 per impression for Canon monochrome equipment and $.0049 black and .059 color for Canon color equipment.

Public comment that night ran heavily against two land questions — the preservation of Parcel 11 and Section 1 property, and the proposed Early Childhood Center on Parcel 16 — with residents from Abington, Terova, Paragon Drive, Bracken Drive and Highbury Drive speaking, including a TSD student. The May 23 special meeting and closed session dealt solely with negotiations, three members participating remotely.

**Business and Other**
Item 8.A sets a public hearing on the proposed 2017-2018 budget for June 20, 2017 at 7:00 p.m. at the Services Building, with the proposed budget available for inspection at the Administration Building from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., June 14 through June 20, and notice published at least six days ahead carrying, in 11-point bold faced type, the statement that the property tax millage rate proposed to be levied will be a subject of the hearing.

Item 10.A is the bond update. The 2013 bond is $125.7 M sold in three series — $59.2 M, $37.2 M and $29.2 M — with construction (including soft costs) taking $45.8 M, $22.5 M and $14.1 M of them and the balance going to furniture, technology, permits, fees and buses. Series 1 construction is 98% complete. The 2017 building projects are Barnard, Bemis and Wass elementary schools, large group instruction space at Larson, the International Academy kitchen, and Athens High School. The roof condition table totals 1,769,050 square feet across the district, of which 543,799 is new including 2017 work and 534,245 is seven or more years old. Including all 2017 projects, the bond has made building improvements at every school, site improvements at 19 of 23 facilities and replaced portions of roofs at 14 of 23.

Agenda packet for the regular meeting of the Troy School District Board of Education, June 6, 2017, 7:00 PM at Athens High School, 4333 John R. The agenda is: 1. Pledge of Allegiance; 2. The cover notes that meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) every Monday and Wednesday at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m. when school is in session, and viewable at http://vimeo.com/troyschools.

**Recognition — athletics.** Item 2.A, read by Mike Jolly, names the All-State Athletes for Winter 2017 with grade, school and sport: Camille Bedford (Athens, synchronized swimming), Michelle Cai, Max Chen (boys swim), Inwoo Cho, Madison Darish (gymnastics), Allen Diao (boys swim), Anna Efstate, Hanna Jung, Kendall Kemp, Yejin Kim, Shannon Li, Sonja Lisowski, Laura Nicholas, Jaclyn Pabalan, Carter Scillion (bowling), Amishi Taneja, Anishka Taneja, Jessie Toomajian, Rohini Verma, Rachel Wu, Christina Xu, Kathleen Young and Aimee Zheng — all but Bedford from Troy High, and all but the swim, bowling and gymnastics entries in synchronized swimming. **Consent agenda (item 5).** A. Minutes of the May 2, 2017 workshop. B. Minutes of the May 16, 2017 meeting. C. Minutes of the May 23, 2017 special meeting. D. Minutes of the May 23, 2017 closed session. E. Second reading and adoption of board policies 2000.04 School District Clubs & Other Activities, 4000.01 Personnel – Labor Negotiation Team, 5000.03 Purchasing – Competitive Bidding & Micro-Purchases, 6000.02 Safety & Security – Firearms & Other Weapons, and 8000.09 General Policies – Web Accessibility Policy. Item 5.E records that the Board Policy Committee reviewed the policies and that the Board's attorney checked them for compliance with State law, the Open Meetings Act and the Revised School Code, the first reading having been conducted at the May 16, 2017 meeting.

**May 2, 2017 workshop minutes.** President Philippart called the workshop to order at 6:00 p.m. at the Administration Building, with Mrs. Fleming, Mr. Gottlieb, Mrs. Hammond, Mr. Hauff, Mr. Miletti and Mr. Schmidt present and administrators Machesky, Birmingham and West in attendance, plus approximately three other members of the audience. Mary Bogush, a Royal Oak resident at 1418 Ottawa, addressed the Board on preservation of Section 1 property. The Business Services update covered board policies, a copier lease for the elementary schools, IA-East and TCCHS, and Section 1 due diligence, for which the Board moved into closed session from 6:35 to 7:45 p.m. Employee Services covered superintendent evaluation tool training with Gary Collins. The meeting adjourned at 9:36 p.m.; Paula Fleming signed as Secretary.

**May 16, 2017 meeting minutes.** Vice-President Schmidt called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. at the Services Building. Present were Fleming, Gottlieb, Hammond and Hauff; Dr. Philippart and Mr. Miletti were absent. Administrators Birmingham, Brzezinski, Cottone, Dziatczak, Griffor, Harris, Morse, Pass, Kwasny, J. Gottlieb, Zendler and West attended, with approximately 150 members of the audience.

The Mission Moment honored teachers Erin Detmer and Natalie Haezebrouck, accepted into the Teachers' College at Columbia University August Writing Institute, a program for educators committed to turning classrooms into richly literate reading and writing workshops that admits only a small number of applicants; Ms. Griffor invited them up to speak. Sixteen nominees were recognized for the Outstanding Support Staff Award: Rose Arnon (Custodian, Costello Elementary), Nahla Asmar (ELD Tutor, Boulan Park), Margaret Baines (Facility Manager, Athens High), Dawn Copp (Health Care Aide, Martell Elementary), Janet Davert (Secretary, Baker Middle), Maxine Japowicz (Paraprofessional, Martell), Janie Kirchler (Health Care Aide, Hamilton Elementary), Sharon Kreza (Secretary, Wattles Elementary), Ivonne Mastracci (Secretary, Troy Union Elementary), Karyn Mroczka (Secretary, Smith Middle), Sue Ohlert (Secretary, Athens High), Joni Pallas (Paraprofessional, Special Education, Larson Middle), Candy Parker (Bus Driver), Erin Prendergast (Para/Resource Room, Troy Union Elementary), Betty Prospal (Secretary/Employee Services) and Seth Wyatt (paraeducator, Special Education, Costello Elementary). Erin Prendergast was named Outstanding Support Staff Employee of the Year and her name was sent to the county for the Betty Campion Outstanding Support Staff Award.

Twenty-six retirees received an engraved clock: Joan Barrett (Troy High, since 1987), Sharon Brennan (Larson Middle, since 1977), Dikki CieChanski (Martell, since 1987), Mary Curl (Secretary, Morse, since 1996), Janet D'Agostino (Secretary, Troy Career Center, since 2000), Vera Dorr (ELD Paraprofessional, Wass/Costello, since 1996), William Edwards (Computer Technician, Services, since 1995), Renee Fidler (Elementary Music, since 1978), Karen Field (Secretary, Athens High, since 1997), Gary Griffith (Troy High, since 1974), Renee Haraburda (Troy High, since 1988), Karen Hurst (Hill Elementary, since 1977), Mary Johnson (Speech Pathologist, Services, since 1991), Mary Klotz (Computer Technician, Schroeder, since 1997), Janet MacDonald (Secretary, Administration Building, since 1987), Susan Madej (Secretary, Martell, since 1999), Gary Mason (Baker Middle, since 1978), Janice Meganck (Secretary, International Academy East, since 1997), Valerie Pfeifer (Troy High, since 1978), Heide Rosenberg (Troy High, since 1991), Sandra Sinnaeve (ELD Paraprofessional, Troy Union, since 2000), Kathleen Steinberger (ELD Paraprofessional, Wattles, since 2001), Hank Thoenes (Boulan Park, since 1987), Colleen Tropea (Smith Middle, since 1985), Camille Tucci (Athens High, since 1986) and Linda Worrell (Troy High, since 1989).

The Board recognized a $10,000 grant from the AT&T Foundation, secured through the Troy Community Foundation and Oakland County Commissioner Doug Tietz, used to provide transportation for high school students in after-school tutoring programs; Tietz and an AT&T Foundation representative were invited to speak. Julie McClure, President of the Troy Foundation for Educational Excellence, was introduced to recognize the year's grant recipients — the Foundation funded 80 grants. A Teacher Appreciation Week resolution for May 8-12, 2017, moved by Mr. Hauff and supported by Mrs. Fleming, passed 5-0 with Miletti and Philippart absent.

Resolution 17-043 approved the April 11, 2017 workshop minutes, the April 18, 2017 meeting minutes, the Treasurer's Report for March 2017 and the Oakland Intermediate School District budget. Resolution 17-044 issued a two-year probationary administrative contract without tenure to Ms. Jessica Carrier as Special Education Supervisor effective July 1, 2017, and 17-045 the same to Ms. Elizabeth Soggs as Director of Technology effective June 5, 2017. Resolution 17-046 authorized the Superintendent or designee to negotiate and execute a Master Equipment Lease Agreement with Great America Financial Services for a fleet of copiers for a period no greater than four years at an annual cost not to exceed $63,690.48 per year, and a cost per copy maintenance agreement with Applied Imaging not to exceed $.0032 per impression for Canon Monochrome equipment and $.0049 black and .059 color per impression for Canon Color equipment for a period not to exceed four years, both as General Fund expenditures. Every vote was 5 yes, 0 no, with Miletti and Philippart absent.

Non-agenda public comment was dominated by land use: Doreen Randall of 5348 Abington and Anne Partlan of 2300 Terova on preservation of Parcel 11; Alex Pitylak of 335 Paragon Drive on the proposed Early Childhood Center/Pre-School; Endi Wu of 313 Bracken Drive and Rachel Wu, a TSD student at the same address, on Parcel 16 and the proposed Early Childhood Development Center; Gordon Schepke of 328 Paragon Drive on the proposed Early Learning Center's construction, funding and approvals; Eileen Heasley of 190 Paragon Drive on the same development; and Larry Cramer of 2360 Highbury Drive on the brightness of lighting and signage at Wass Elementary. Under Other, the Board took a first reading of the five policies later adopted at this June meeting. Student representatives reported: Pranathi Locula (Troy High) on prom at Cherry Creek Golf Club; Parker Gilchrist (Troy College & Career) on students and staff volunteering to replace mulch and clear debris, plans for the school's first-ever prom, and an Alex & Ani fundraiser at Partridge Creek returning 15% of sales profits for scholarships; Lauren Hanoosh (Athens, filling in for Ellory Thill) on prom at Andiamos on May 6th, student council presenting Charity Week to L'Anse Creuse North Schools, which plans to adopt it, Senior Honors night on June 6th and commencement on June 10th at 3:30 p.m.; and Aman Agrawal (International Academy-East) on Honors Night on April 26, a "Night at Gatsby's" prom on April 27th, capstone projects, three weeks of IB exams and a June 16th last day. In board comments Mr. Hauff described classroom visits at Barnard Elementary; Mrs. Hammond encouraged involvement in the Diversity & Inclusion Council; Mrs. Gottlieb spoke to the district's Journey to be World Class by 2020; Mrs. Fleming announced the Troy Foundation for Educational Excellence golf outing on Friday, August 25th; and Dr. Machesky thanked the City of Troy for hosting the district-wide art show at the Troy Community Center and announced the next Chat with the Superintendent. Mr. Schmidt noted the next meeting at Athens on June 6th and a workshop on June 13th. The meeting adjourned at 8:59 p.m.

**May 23, 2017 special meeting and closed session.** Vice-President Schmidt called the special meeting to order at 5:30 p.m. at the Administration Building with Fleming, Gottlieb and Hauff present; Dr. Philippart, Mrs. Hammond and Mr. Miletti were planning to participate remotely in the closed session. Superintendent Machesky attended with Rick West, Dave Pass, Jordan Harris and Mark Dziatczak; there were no members of the audience. Resolution 17-047, moved by Mrs. Fleming and supported by Mr. Hauff, took the Board into closed session to discuss negotiations as permitted by the Michigan Open Meetings Act, Public Act 267, Section 8(c), on a roll call of Hauff yes, Miletti absent, Philippart absent, Schmidt yes, Fleming yes, Gottlieb yes, Hammond absent. The Board moved to closed session at 5:30 p.m. and reconvened at 5:32 p.m., adjourning at 6:55 p.m. The separate closed session minutes record Schmidt calling it to order at 5:32 p.m. with Fleming, Gottlieb and Hauff present and Philippart, Hammond and Miletti participating remotely, Machesky attending with Harris, Pass, Dziatczak and West, and no business conducted other than discussing negotiations.

**Business: budget public hearing.** Item 8.A recites that Michigan law requires every local unit of government, including a school district, to hold a public hearing on its proposed budget with notice at least six days before; that the notice must give the time and place and state where the proposed budget may be inspected; that it must carry, in 11-point bold faced type, "THE PROPERTY TAX MILLAGE RATE PROPOSED TO BE LEVIED TO SUPPORT THE PROPOSED BUDGET WILL BE A SUBJECT OF THIS HEARING"; and that the hearing must precede final adoption. It resolves that a public hearing be held on June 20, 2017 at a regular Board meeting beginning at 7:00 p.m. at the Troy School District Services Building, 4420 Livernois Road, Troy 48098, and authorizes the Secretary to publish notice in substantially the form of Exhibit A. Exhibit A states that copies of the proposed budget will be available at the Administration Building, 4400 Livernois, from 8:00 a.m. until 5:00 p.m., Wednesday, June 14, 2017 through Tuesday, June 20, 2017, and is signed by Paula Fleming, Secretary.

**Other: bond projects update.** The presentation covers the 2013 bond issue, $125.7 M to be sold in three series. Series 1 is $59.2 M, Series 2 $37.2 M and Series 3 $29.2 M; construction including soft costs accounts for $45.8 M, $22.5 M and $14.1 M respectively, with $10 M, $8.5 M and $8.5 M going to furniture, technology and permits, fees and buses. Series 1 construction, at $45.8 M, is 98% complete. Construction is finished at Barnard, Bemis, Costello, Hamilton, Hill, Leonard, Martell, Morse, Schroeder, Troy Union, Wass, Wattles, Baker, Boulan, Larson, Smith, Troy High and IAE, with Athens High partially complete across 2016 and 2017. The 2017 building projects are Barnard, Bemis and Wass elementary schools, large group instruction space at Larson Middle School, the International Academy kitchen, and Athens High School. Sitework falls into four categories — traffic flow needs for bus and parent drop-off, paving reconstruction and replacement, concrete and sidewalk replacement, and site lighting upgrades. Roofing is either restoration (partial replacement, refurbishment or repair from the General Fund) or remove and replace. The 2016 roof condition table gives total square footage of 1,769,050, of which 543,799 is new including 2017 work, 234,031 is one to three years old, 456,975 is four to six years old and 534,245 is seven or more years old; the largest single roofs are Troy High at 250,250 square feet and Athens at 210,480, followed by Boulan and Larson at 105,000 each and Smith at 97,075. The summary states that including all 2017 projects the bond has made building improvements at every school, site improvements at 19 of 23 facilities, and replaced portions of roofs at 14 of 23 facilities.
